description: Somos NASQARQ, un equipo de arquitectos e investigadores peruanos que explora cómo nuestros paisajes pueden servir como análogos de la Luna y Marte. Aportamos diagnóstico territorial, análisis de sitio, modelado 3D, diseño y visualización para transformar datos científicos en conocimiento espacial. Buscamos colaboradores con habilidades en programación, desarrollo web, IA aplicada al análisis de datos. Desde el Perú, exploremos la Tierra para descubrir las posibilidades de otros mundos!
summary:
NASQARQ is a web platform that helps prepare for future lunar bases. Since no place on Earth replicates all lunar conditions, instead of searching for a perfect analog, it proposes a set of two to four complementary locations, each useful for testing a different function of a base.

To achieve this, it integrates NASA and ESA satellite data into 15 km cells and compares seven dimensions, ranging from topography and temperature to resources and subsurface characteristics. Building on this foundation, it applies Machine Learning to distinguish both environments (Random Forest), select the most informative variables (XGBoost), and fill in missing lunar data (HistGradientBoosting). It then calculates similarities, optimizes each combination, and identifies the gaps that Earth cannot reproduce.

The results support this approach. For 8,104 lunar sites, it found 4,096 analogs, 95% of them new, and in 400 evaluated points, it achieved lower physical error than a baseline in 82% of cases, with sites an average of 118 km from populated areas. Everything is explored through a web interface featuring 3D simulation, and the analysis uses Python, Scikit-learn, and XGBoost.
details:
NASQARQ identifies Earth locations that resemble lunar sites (terrestrial analogs) for future permanent lunar base operations. The platform processes open satellite datasets, primarily from NASA missions, and organizes them into approximately 15 km spatial grid cells.

Dataset Coverage

Moon

  • 129,600 grid cells (0.5° resolution) across the South and East lunar regions.
  • 72,198 buildable cells suitable for infrastructure deployment.

Earth

  • 661,509 terrestrial land cells.
  • 264,069 buildable cells suitable for analog site evaluation.

Machine Learning Pipeline

Machine Learning models are used to identify relevant features, eliminate redundant variables, and impute missing data. The Earth-Moon comparison framework evaluates both bodies across seven operational dimensions:

  1. Topography and terrain morphology
  2. Thermal and illumination conditions
  3. Geology and material composition
  4. Surface processes
  5. Water and resource availability
  6. Landing, mobility, and construction suitability
  7. Subsurface characteristics

Each dimension combines three evaluation factors:

  • Relative pattern similarity
  • Physical similarity
  • Data confidence

Multi-Analog Campaign Strategy

Instead of searching for a single "best" terrestrial analog, NASQARQ generates a complementary analog campaign for each lunar site.

Each analog location is assigned to the lunar base function it reproduces most effectively, such as:

  • Habitat deployment
  • Landing pad operations
  • Resource extraction systems
  • Inter-module transportation corridors
  • Scientific research activities

Web Platform Capabilities

The web platform allows users to:

  • Explore 8,104 lunar locations, including Shackleton, Malapert, Tycho, and Apollo 11 sites.
  • Visualize terrestrial analogs using NASA Worldview imagery.
  • Compare campaign-level coverage against the performance of the single highest-ranked analog.
  • Inspect the distance from each analog location to the nearest populated settlement and to the nearest known analog site.

Gap Analysis

The platform includes a gap-analysis module that explains whether discrepancies between a lunar site and its terrestrial analog are caused by:

  • Physical differences
  • Pattern mismatches
  • Data limitations

Parallel 3D Simulation Environment

NASQARQ provides a synchronized 3D simulation environment for both the Moon and its selected terrestrial analog.

Users can:

  • Deploy lunar base modules.
    • Solar storms
    • Micrometeorite impacts
    • Seismic activity
    • Eclipses
    • Sandstorms

The simulator also enables side-by-side comparison of key operational metrics throughout a lunar day, including:

  • Temperature
  • Gravity
  • Atmospheric pressure
  • Solar energy availability

Benefits

NASQARQ automates the processing and comparison of large-scale geospatial datasets from two celestial bodies.

Compared with the reference analog approach, the platform:

  • Identifies analog sites with lower physical error in 82% of evaluated lunar locations.
  • Reduces the median distance to the nearest settlement from 220 km to 118 km, improving logistical accessibility.
  • Proposes previously unexplored analog environments, with 95% of highlighted analogs (4,096 unique locations) situated more than 500 km from the known analog sites considered in the study.

Expected Impact

NASQARQ contributes to scientific research and future lunar mission preparation through a reproducible methodology for terrestrial analog discovery.

The framework supports:

  • Identification of Earth-based lunar analog environments.
    • Vacuum conditions
    • One-sixth lunar gravity
    • Space radiation exposure
    • Space weathering
    • Impact-generated regolith
    • Extreme thermal cycles

Technology Stack

Programming Languages and Libraries

  • Python 3.12
  • Scikit-learn
  • XGBoost
  • PyTorch
  • NumPy
  • Pandas
  • SciPy
  • Earthaccess
  • OPeNDAP
  • PyHDF
  • H5py
  • PyArrow

Hardware

  • NVIDIA RTX 3060 GPU

Machine Learning Models and Algorithms

  • Random Forest
  • k-Nearest Neighbors (kNN)
  • HistGradientBoosting
  • Autoencoder-based feature learning
  • Hierarchical Clustering
  • Greedy Selection Algorithm

Methodology

  • CRISP-DM (Cross-Industry Standard Process for Data Mining)

Lunar Data Sources

  • Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LOLA, Diviner, LEND, LAMP)
  • GRAIL
  • Lunar Prospector
  • SELENE (Kaguya)

Earth Data Sources

  • SRTM
  • MODIS
  • ASTER GED
  • GLDAS
  • MERRA-2
  • NASA POWER
  • SEDAC GPWv4
  • ESA CCI Permafrost

Platform Architecture

  • Web application
  • REST API
  • Database backend
  • 3D visualization engine
  • NASA Worldview integration
